subject: Warning only when trying to label variances

messages.author: c1d90967b611a5b6
messages.subject: Warning only when trying to label variances
parts:
Greetings. I have a model that runs without issue unless I try to label the variances, in which case a warning about the vcov matrix not being positive definite occurs. Perhaps I'm unintentionally modifying a constraint?

I have commented out the offending lines below:

lavmod <- '
Commit  =~ a*q0051_0001+b*q0051_0002+c*q0051_0003+d*q0051_0004
Commitp =~ a*q0051_0001par+b*q0051_0002par+c*q0051_0003par+d*q0051_0004par
q0051_0001    | q1t1*t1 + q1t2*t2
q0051_0001par | q1t1*t1 + q1t2*t2
q0051_0002    | q2t1*t1 + q2t2*t2
q0051_0002par | q2t1*t1 + q2t2*t2
q0051_0003    | q3t1*t1 + q3t2*t2
q0051_0003par | q3t1*t1 + q3t2*t2
q0051_0004    | q4t1*t1 + q4t2*t2
q0051_0004par | q4t1*t1 + q4t2*t2
Commit  ~~ cv*Commit
Commitp ~~ cv*Commitp
Commit  ~~ Commitp
#q0051_0001    ~~ v1*q0051_0001
#q0051_0001par ~~ vp1*q0051_0001par
#q0051_0002    ~~ v2*q0051_0002
#q0051_0002par ~~ vp2*q0051_0002par
#q0051_0003    ~~ v3*q0051_0003
#q0051_0003par ~~ vp3*q0051_0003par
#q0051_0004    ~~ v4*q0051_0004
#q0051_0004par ~~ vp4*q0051_0004par
'

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Warning only when trying to label variances
parts: I have a model that runs without issue unless I try to label the variances, in which case a warning about the vcov matrix not being positive definite occurs. Perhaps I'm unintentionally modifying a constraint?

It is hard to know without seeing your lavaan() call.  Since your syntax is labeling residual variances of categorical indicators, I assume you are setting parameterization = "theta", because the default ("delta") setting does not allow residual variances to be fixed/freed, only the scaling factors.

https://www.statmodel.com/download/webnotes/CatMGLong.pdf

You will notice if you compare their parameter tables (e.g., parTable() output) that specifying the residual variances frees them.  

lavmod <- '

Commit  =~ a*q0051_0001+b*q0051_0002+c*q0051_0003+d*q0051_0004
Commitp =~ a*q0051_0001par+b*q0051_0002par+c*q0051_0003par+d*q0051_0004par
q0051_0001    | q1t1*t1 + q1t2*t2
q0051_0001par | q1t1*t1 + q1t2*t2
q0051_0002    | q2t1*t1 + q2t2*t2
q0051_0002par | q2t1*t1 + q2t2*t2
q0051_0003    | q3t1*t1 + q3t2*t2
q0051_0003par | q3t1*t1 + q3t2*t2
q0051_0004    | q4t1*t1 + q4t2*t2
q0051_0004par | q4t1*t1 + q4t2*t2
Commit  ~~ cv*Commit
Commitp ~~ cv*Commitp
Commit  ~~ Commitp

q0051_0001    ~~ v1*q0051_0001
q0051_0001par ~~ vp1*q0051_0001par
q0051_0002    ~~ v2*q0051_0002
q0051_0002par ~~ vp2*q0051_0002par
q0051_0003    ~~ v3*q0051_0003
q0051_0003par ~~ vp3*q0051_0003par
q0051_0004    ~~ v4*q0051_0004
q0051_0004par ~~ vp4*q0051_0004par
'
lavaanify(lavmod, parameterization = "theta", std.lv = TRUE)

Those residual variances are not all identifiable.  Without constraints, they are fixed to 1 by default (or implicitly set to 1 minus the explained variance, if parameterization = "delta").  With the equality constraints on the 2 thresholds, then you can identify them by setting only one set to 1 (e.g., either the Commit or the Commitp indicators) and free the other set.

q0051_0001    ~~  1*q0051_0001
q0051_0001par ~~ NA*q0051_0001par
q0051_0002    ~~  1*q0051_0002
q0051_0002par ~~ NA*q0051_0002par
q0051_0003    ~~  1*q0051_0003
q0051_0003par ~~ NA*q0051_0003par
q0051_0004    ~~  1*q0051_0004
q0051_0004par ~~ NA*q0051_0004par

If you want to subsequently test strict invariance by constraining residual variances to equality, then you simply set them all back to 1 again (which will be done by default if you don't specify them in the syntax).

FYI, the intercepts are also fixed to zero for identification, and that identification constraint can also be freed when you constrain at least one threshold to equality.  

q0051_0001    ~  0*1
q0051_0001par ~ NA*1
q0051_0002    ~  0*1
q0051_0002par ~ NA*1
q0051_0003    ~  0*1
q0051_0003par ~ NA*1
q0051_0004    ~  0*1
q0051_0004par ~ NA*1

Since you only have 3-category data, you can't actually test whether thresholds are equal except on the condition that intercepts and residual variances are equal.  Wu and Estabrook (2016) recommend starting with thresholds constrained to equality as the configural model, with free loadings and free intercepts and residual variances in all but the reference group/occasion (e.g., the first group or repeated measure).

https://doi.org/10.1007/s11336-016-9506-0
